Date: 2026-03-27 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: John Mills (Redwood AE), Sara Chen (Redwood SE), Mark Alvarez (Greenline CTO), Priya Rao (Greenline Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Greenline Platform)
Recorded on: Fireflies.ai
Notes: Demo focused on rate limits, quotas, and org/project key model for multi-tenant controls
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a product walkthrough of rate limiting, org and project API keys, and quota controls in the Redwood Console and API. Greenline is evaluating a Dedicated or Private deployment for multi-tenant usage across ten internal products. Key concerns: per-tenant quotas, predictable cost, SSO/SAML for team access, audit logs, and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share pricing/pilot agreement and technical docs, customer to provide tenant list and throughput estimates, schedule pilot kickoff and benchmark.
topics: Overview of org vs project keys
Rate limiting and quota strategies (global vs per-project)
Console demo: creating org, projects, assigning keys
API demo: header usage, key rotation, scoped keys
Dedicated vs Hosted considerations for multi-tenant isolation
Security controls: RBAC, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS
transcript:
[00:00] John Mills: All right everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna get started. I'm John from Redwood, AE on the account. Sara my teammate is the SE, she'll do most of the console demo.
[00:12] Mark Alvarez: Hi John, thanks. We have Priya and Liam on as well. Priya's leading the AI workstream, Liam runs infra.
[00:20] Sara Chen: Hi team, quick agenda: we'll cover org and project keys, how rate limits and quotas work, show the console, then a short API example and Q/A. Please interrupt if anything is unclear.
[00:34] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Our big ask is being able to enforce per-tenant quotas and also keep cost predictable — we run across 10 product teams and need isolation.
[00:46] John Mills: Totally. Narrowing that down: are you planning on hosted Redwood or dedicated/private? That changes how we think about isolation.
[00:56] Mark Alvarez: We're leaning towards Dedicated or Private. Compliance and data residency are important. But we'd like the hosted flow if the economics make sense.
[01:08] Sara Chen: Got it. For both Dedicated and Hosted, we have the concept of an 'org' and 'projects' underneath it. Org is the billing and admin boundary, projects map to your tenant boundaries for keys and quotas.
[01:22] Liam O'Connor: Can we do per-project QPS limits and token quotas? And throttle per API key?
[01:30] Sara Chen: Yes — you can set rate limits on the org level, project level, and on individual API keys. The Console shows a default quota of tokens per month per project, and you can also apply a burst QPS limit.
[01:44] John Mills: Useful to note we support both token-based quotas (monthly or rolling window) and request/QPS-based throttling. Plus you can combine them. For example: project A gets 300k tokens/month and 50 rps burst, project B gets 50k tokens/month.
[02:05] Priya Rao: How does this interact with batching and caching at the runtime? We don't want our tenant to get unfair caching benefits or cold-start latencies.
[02:15] Sara Chen: Great question. Our runtime has workload-aware batching and prefix/KV caching. Rate limits are applied at the ingress layer before batching, so quotas prevent overuse. We also have policies to reserve capacity for higher-tier projects so they don't get impacted by noisy neighbors.
[02:33] Mark Alvarez: Can you demo creating projects and keys?
[02:37] Sara Chen: Yep. Switching to the console — sorry audio may be a bit low, let me zoom the screen.
[02:45] [screen share noises]
[02:50] Sara Chen: Here's the org page, you can see billing settings, org-wide rate limit, and project list. I'll create a new project called 'patient-notes' and show key scoping.
[03:05] Sara Chen: Create project -> name -> select quota template. We have templates (dev, prod, enterprise) and you can customize tokens/month, max-context-length, and QPS.
[03:18] John Mills: Templates are just starting points — you can programmatically update via the API as well.
[03:24] [03:30] Priya Rao: If we rotate keys, does the old key immediately stop? We need seamless rotation for our apps.
[03:37] Sara Chen: You can do staged rotation — create a new key, deploy, then revoke the old one. There's a key-rotation endpoint and the Console gives a one-click rotate flow.
[03:48] Liam O'Connor: What about limited-scoped keys — say read-only or only embeddings?
[03:53] Sara Chen: We support scoped keys; you can scope by permission (generate, embeddings, admin), by project, and by expiration. Good for client-side use where you want to limit operations.
[04:07] Mark Alvarez: How do you separate logs and telemetry per tenant? We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and separate usage reporting per project.
[04:17] Sara Chen: Audit logs and usage are per-project. You can export logs to S3 or to our syslog/forwarder. We also support per-project cost breakdowns in the console, token-level attribution, and trace IDs for requests.
[04:33] Priya Rao: Does Redwood support SSO SAML? We need to tie into Okta and map groups to RBAC.
[04:40] John Mills: Yes, SAML/SSO is supported. You can map IdP groups to roles in the Console — admin, billing, viewer, developer. For private deployments we also integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management.
[04:56] [05:00] Liam O'Connor: About KMS — do you support AWS KMS and Google KMS? Any HSM work?
[05:06] Sara Chen: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and an HSM option for Private deployments. All audit logs and data-at-rest encryption are compatible with those keys.
[05:16] Mark Alvarez: Ok good. Let's talk about enforcement: if a project exceeds token quota mid-run, do you fail the request or degrade gracefully?
[05:26] Sara Chen: You can configure enforcement policies. Options are: hard deny (429), soft limit with warning headers and a grace buffer (allow but flag), or fallback to a lower-cost model variant for degraded quality. We often recommend a grace buffer for user-facing workloads.
[05:44] Priya Rao: Can Redwood do automatic fallback to a quantized/cheaper model when a project's quota is reached?
[05:52] John Mills: Yes — we can route to model variants based on policy. So when quota hits a threshold, requests can target a compatible quantized model or a lower parameter model to stay within cost targets.
[06:05] [06:10] Sara Chen: API example: header x-redwood-key: project_x_key. You can also use org-level keys for cross-project admin calls. For scoped calls, we validate key -> project mapping then apply per-key limits.
[06:24] Liam O'Connor: Is there rate limiting at token-level or request-level in the API?
[06:29] Sara Chen: Both. Token rate limiting prevents token bursts; request/QPS rate limiting prevents request floods. In practice we use both to stop abuse and preserve latency SLOs.
[06:40] Mark Alvarez: For the dedicated/private case, how much separation do we get between projects? Do we get separate GPU pools or is it logical isolation?
[06:50] John Mills: For Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools for your org. Projects are logically isolated within your org but we can carve out node pools per project if you want physical isolation. For Private, you control the infra so you get full separation.
[07:07] Priya Rao: What's the on-boarding timeline for a pilot? We have legal/compliance review to finish, but want to start a 2-week pilot for benchmarking.
[07:16] John Mills: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. We usually do an initial 1-hour kickoff, then 2 weeks of testing with a shared dashboard. We'll need expected QPS and a sample dataset to simulate traffic.
[07:29] Sara Chen: We'll also run a perf benchmark with your sample prompts to show latency and cost per token across model variants.
[07:36] Mark Alvarez: Can you share an example benchmark spreadsheet?
[07:40] Sara Chen: Yes, I'll share our benchmark template and an example from a similar healthcare customer — redacted — after the call.
[07:48] [08:00] Priya Rao: Security docs — SOC2, ISO — can you send those? Also a data flow diagram for Private deployment.
[08:06] John Mills: We'll include SOC 2 attestation, encryption and KMS docs, and a network topology example for Private.
[08:13] Liam O'Connor: One more question on quotas: can we set daily burst limits per project in addition to monthly tokens? We want to throttle bad actors fast.
[08:22] Sara Chen: Yes, you can layer windows — per-second QPS, per-minute, per-hour, per-day, plus monthly token budget. Alerts can be configured at thresholds.
[08:33] Mark Alvarez: Great. Competitor question: how is this different from the CloudX managed endpoints?
[08:38] John Mills: Two big differences: production-first operational tooling with per-token attribution and rollouts, and the ability to run the same control plane across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Also deeper cost-optimization tooling — Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quant and fallback policies.
[08:55] Priya Rao: Is Redwood Optimize a separate add-on?
[08:58] John Mills: It's an add-on with an initial free trial for pilots, and then usage-based or subscription pricing depending on retention and advanced features.
[09:07] [09:12] Sara Chen: Back to the console — I'll show the key rotation flow and the API call for setting a project quota.
[09:20] Sara Chen: Here's the API curl sample: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/project_id/quota -H 'Authorization: Bearer ORG_KEY' -d '{"tokens_month":300000, "qps":50}'.
[09:36] Priya Rao: Nice. For telemetry, will we get a per-request trace id to tie to our logs?
[09:42] Sara Chen: Yes we return X-Request-ID and you can inject your trace context. We also provide a trace link in the console to inspect latency and model choice.
[09:54] Liam O'Connor: How do we automate creating projects and keys? We want to provision a new project per customer automatically.
[10:02] John Mills: There's a projects API to create and provision keys, plus webhooks for quota alarms. Most customers do a Terraform module or call our API in their onboarding pipeline.
[10:14] Priya Rao: Are there SDKs for key management?
[10:18] Sara Chen: We have official SDKs (Python, Node) and REST examples. SDKs include helper methods for rotation and scoped key creation.
[10:25] Mark Alvarez: Any gotchas around rate limiting and regional routing? We have users in EU and US.
[10:31] Sara Chen: You can set region-specific policies and route by region. If using Hosted, requests can be routed to the nearest region with fallback. For Dedicated, you pick region pools. Rate limiting follows the region unless you set global quotas.
[10:45] [11:00] John Mills: Ok I think we're close to wrap. Recap: Sara to send console screenshots, key rotation doc, and benchmark template. I'll send pricing and pilot agreement. Greenline to send tenant/project list and throughput estimates. We'll aim to run pilot week of April 7.
[11:17] Priya Rao: That works. One final note: we'll need a redlined data processing addendum for privacy — legal will reach out.
[11:25] John Mills: Understood, legal to legal. We'll include our DPA and SOC2 in the package.
[11:32] Mark Alvarez: Thanks everyone, that was very helpful.
[11:36] John Mills: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[11:42] [call end]
